Finally, simplify your answer. This method is systematic and reliable.

To find stationary points of y=f(x), first differentiate f(x) to get f '(x). Set f '(x)=0 to locate potential stationary points. Then, solve for x. After finding the x-values, substitute back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-coordinates. Optionally, use the second derivative test to classify each point as a minimum, maximum, or point of inflection.
